'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
***[[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|ISIL–K]] leader Mawlawi Ziya ul-Haq is killed and more than 80 fighters are arrested during [[Taliban]] raids in the eastern [[Nangarhar Province]]. The raids are carried out as ISIL-K has killed several people during attacks in [[Jalalabad]] in recent days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/27/afghanistan-taliban-promises-to-eradicate-groups-seeking-chaos (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**A [[Tanzania]]n soldier is killed while two more Tanzanian and a [[Lesotho]] soldiers are wounded after storming an [[Islamic State|ISIL]]-linked groups hideout in [[Cabo Delgado]], [[Mozambique]]. [https://www.mmegi.bw/news/tanzanian-soldier-confirmed-as-fatality-in-sadc-forces-raid-in-mozambique/news (Mmegi)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Ten [[FARC dissidents]] are killed during a [[Military Forces of Colombia|military]] bombing in [[Morichal Nuevo]], [[Guainía Department]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/least-10-farc-dissidents-killed-colombia-bombing-military-says-2021-09-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021 United Kingdom fuel panic buying]]
**The [[Government of the United Kingdom|government]] places the [[British Army|army]] on standby to help deliver [[Motor fuel|fuel]] to [[petrol station]]s if it becomes necessary after [[panic buying]] has depleted their stocks. The increased demand arose after press reports that the ongoing delivery driver shortage could reduce the availability of fuel. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-58713770 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Cumbre Vieja volcanic eruption]]
**The [[Cumbre Vieja]] [[volcano]] becomes highly active again after two periods during the day with no emission of ash and lava. [https://elpais.com/sociedad/2021-09-27/el-volcan-de-la-palma-deja-de-expulsar-lava-pero-la-colada-sigue-avanzando-hacia-el-mar.html (''El País'')]
*[[2021 Arkalochori earthquake|2021 Crete earthquake]]
**A 5.8 magnitude [[list of earthquakes in Greece|earthquake]] strikes the [[Greek island]] of [[Crete]], killing one person and injuring 35 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/earthquake-magnitude-56-strikes-crete-greece-emsc-2021-09-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[Power outage]]s are reported in the [[Northeast China]] [[provinces of China|provinces]] of [[Liaoning]], [[Jilin]], and [[Heilongjiang]]. Local media said that the cause of the outages was an increase in coal prices. The [[State Grid Corporation of China]] said that it would take comprehensive measures to ensure an adequate power supply for people's basic needs and try its best to avoid power cuts. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-58704221 (BBC News)] [http://www.news.cn/english/2021-09/27/c_1310212994.htm (Xinhuanet)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****The [[Ministry of Health, Labour, and Welfare|Health Ministry]] panel committee approve the usage of the single-dose monoclonal antibody-based treatment [[sotrovimab]] developed by [[GlaxoSmithKline]] and Vir Biotechnology to treat mild and moderately-ill [[COVID-19]] patients. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/09/27/national/science-health/sotrovimab-japan-panel-approval/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Jordan]]
****[[Hussein, Crown Prince of Jordan]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1936436/middle-east (Arab News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 19 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,152. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-09/27/c_1310212814.htm (Xinhuanet)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] limits the maximum group sizes for social gatherings and dine-ins at restaurants and bars to two people as well as defaulting to [[work from home]] in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. These restrictions will remain in effect until October 24. [https://sbr.com.sg/healthcare/news/social-interactions-cut-anew-slow-covid-19-infections (Singapore Business Review)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***The U.S. surpasses 43 million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.fox23.com/news/trending/coronavirus-total-us-covid-19-cases-top-43-million/KTLMWMNB3BDW3DNJZQM6HWXV6A/ (KOKI-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vermont]]
*****People over the age of 75 in [[Vermont]] can now register to receive a booster shot of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-health-vermont-22ff16c8c77702d29192f135d973f186 (AP)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****[[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]] receives his third dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/09/27/biden-to-receive-covid-booster-shot-live-on-camera-monday.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***The government announces that the [[state of emergency|state of catastrophe]] and the night [[curfew]] in the country will end on October 1. [https://www.cooperativa.cl/noticias/sociedad/salud/coronavirus/se-acaba-el-toque-de-queda-gobierno-no-renovara-el-estado-de-catastrofe/2021-09-27/132920.html (Cooperativa.cl)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Hungary–Russia relations]], [[Hungary–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Hungary]] and [[Russia]] sign a [[natural gas]] supply deal which will see [[Gazprom]] supply Hungary with 4.5 billion cubic metres of gas annually via [[Serbia]] and [[Austria]] for the next 15 years. Ukraine criticizes the gas pact, saying that it is a "purely political, economically unreasonable decision". In response, Hungarian Foreign Minister [[Péter Szijjártó]] accuses Ukraine of "meddling" in its internal affairs. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/hungary-russias-gazprom-expected-sign-new-long-term-gas-supply-deal-monday-2021-09-27/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Taliban offensive]], [[Foreign relations of Afghanistan]]
**[[Permanent Representative of Afghanistan to the United Nations|Afghanistan's permanent representative to the United Nations]] Ghulam Isaczai withdraws from the list of speakers at the [[United Nations General Assembly]]. The move comes after the [[Taliban]] nominated a delegation to represent [[Afghanistan]] at the [[United Nations]], although the UN continues to recognize the [[Ashraf Ghani]]-led [[government of Afghanistan|government]] as [[Permanent Mission of Afghanistan to the United Nations|the country's permanent mission]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1648781 (AFP via ''Dawn'')]
*[[South Sudan–Sudan relations]]
**[[Sudan]] resumes its [[import]]ation of oil from neighboring [[South Sudan]], which was temporarily halted due to [[War in Darfur|Darfur War]]-related protests blocking access to [[Port Sudan]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20210927-south-sudan-oil-exports-resume-after-khartoum-protesters-deal (AFP via Radio France Internationale)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Poland]]
**Three regions in [[Poland]] repeal their status as an "[[LGBT-free zone]]" after pressure from the [[European Commission]] and activists. The declaration of "free of [[LGBT]] ideology" had been imposed in 2019 under heavy pressure from [[Catholic Church|Catholic]] conservatives in the regions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/two-polish-regions-repeal-lgbt-free-declarations-2021-09-27/ (Reuters)]
*American singer [[R. Kelly]] is found guilty of [[racketeering]] and [[sex trafficking]] over a two-decade period. [https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-58714203 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Swiss same-sex marriage referendum]], [[LGBT rights in Switzerland]]
**Official results show that the "yes" campaign won and that [[same-sex marriage]] will be legalized in [[Switzerland]]. Results show 64.1% voting yes with 35.9% voting no. [https://www.dw.com/en/swiss-vote-yes-to-same-sex-marriage/a-59313074 (Deutsche Welle)]
*[[2019 Bougainvillean independence referendum]]
**Bougainvilleans are consulted by [[President of the Autonomous Region of Bougainville|president]] [[Ishmael Toroama]] as to where the capital of [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|Bougainville]] should be located once the [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|region]] achieves full independence from [[Papua New Guinea]]. Currently, the capital is [[Buka, Papua New Guinea|Buka]] but this was always considered temporary due to the [[Bougainville conflict|civil war]]. The strongest push is for [[Arawa, Bougainville|Arawa]] to be designated as the capital. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/452411/bougainvilleans-consulted-on-location-for-new-capital (RNZ)]
*[[2021 Haitian general election]], [[2021 Haitian constitutional referendum]], [[2018–2021 Haitian protests]]
**The [[Provisional Electoral Council]] postpones indefinitely the election and constitutional referendum for a third time, targeting 7 November 2021, after [[Prime Minister of Haiti|Prime Minister]] [[Ariel Henry]] dismissed several members of the council. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1494038/haiti-elections-postponed-indefinitely-amid-crisis (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[2021 Sammarinese abortion referendum]], [[Abortion in San Marino]]
**After a final tally of votes from yesterday's referendum establishes a majority of 77%, [[abortion]] at up to 12 weeks of pregnancy is [[Legalization of abortion|legalized]] in [[San Marino]]. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-09-27/san-marino-legalizes-abortion-pope-womens-groups-disagree (Associated Press)]

'''Sports'''
*[[UEFA]] announces that it has abandoned and nullified its disciplinary cases against [[association football|football]] clubs [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Juventus F.C.|Juventus]], and [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] over their commitment to the controversial [[European Super League]], following a [[Madrid]] court ruling. UEFA also says that it will not request payment of the sums offered by the nine other founding clubs. [https://www.nst.com.my/sports/football/2021/09/731495/uefa-drops-case-against-european-super-league-rebels (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]
